content:
The test image shows a **stem** split open longitudinally, revealing:
- Bleached/tan dried interior tissue
- Dark grayish-black hard structures (sclerotia) embedded within the stem
- Outer stem browning

This strongly matches **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** — the description specifically says "positive identification achieved by slicing the diseased stem longitudinally" with "hard, grayish-black sclerotia about the size of a plump grain of rice embedded within the stem tissue."

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image confirms this perfectly. Both images are from the same Bugwood series (5593844 vs 5593851), showing the same stem:
- Exterior view (reference): bleached stem with dark sclerotia visible on surface, same black plastic mulch background
- Interior view (test): stem split open revealing bleached internal tissue with embedded dark sclerotia

This is a textbook Sclerotinia timber rot presentation — longitudinal stem slice showing sclerotia, exactly as described in the diagnostic criteria.
